detector_calibrate — DRIVE pxrd op

• Data kinds: image2d × signal × table → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.detector_calibrate(image, d_spacings, geometry_guess, n_azimuth=180, fit_tilt=True, min_rings=2) (to call the implementation directly, import pxrd; pxrd.detector_calibrate(image, d_spacings, geometry_guess, n_azimuth=180, fit_tilt=True, min_rings=2); from the registry, opsdrive.get("detector_calibrate"))

Usage

Calibrates the detector center, distance and tilt from the rings of a known standard (such as Si).

d_spacings is a list of standard spacings [Å] (not necessarily in order of strength), geometry_guess is at least pixel and

wavelength, if known, cx, cy, distance, tilt, tilt_dir. Steps:

1. If there is no center, start from the center of gravity of the bright pixel, pick up the strongest ring along the ray, and update the center three times by fitting the circle.

2. If there is no distance, assign the first peak of the radial profile to the candidates for d (four from the smallest 2θ) and compare them with the predictions for the other rings. Select the pair with the highest number of matching observations.

3. Predict the position of each ring on the n_azimuth rays in the current geometry, pick a point at the center of gravity of the intensity in the window, Use scipy.optimize.least_squares to guess (two components of cx, cy, distance, tilt) with the 2θ residual [deg]. window 4 times while contracting. The tilt is solved using the two components of the rotation vector tilt·(cos φ, sin φ) (avoiding the singularity where φ becomes indeterminate when the slope is 0).

Return value (dict): Geometry (cx, cy, distance, pixel, wavelength, tilt, tilt_dir)

rms_two_theta_deg・n_points・n_rings・rings_deg・ok(rms is less than 0.25·pixel/distance

and rings >= min_rings).

Raises ValueError: Image not 2-D, no d's, no pixels/wavelengths, ``min_rings'' rings not found.
